elements: Panel a) — horizontal black x1 axis line with cone arrowheads at both ends, italic label 'x₁' immediately beside the right arrow tip
Panel a) — solid black dot at the origin of the x1 axis (the 0-dimensional 'hyperplane' point)
Panel a) — short vertical teal bar centered on the origin dot marking the decision point where w₁x₁ + b = 0
Panel b) — black x1 axis (horizontal, arrowheads both ends) with italic 'x₁' beside the right arrow tip; black x2 axis (vertical, arrowheads both ends) with italic 'x₂' beside the top arrow tip
Panel b) — black dot at origin
Panel b) — teal line through the origin (hyperplane of neuron 1, default x₁ = 0, drawn lying on the x2 axis)
Panel b) — terracotta/orange line through the origin (hyperplane of neuron 2, default x₂ = 0, drawn lying on the x1 axis)

Panel c) — three black coordinate axes through the origin: x1 to screen-right (arrow tip labeled 'x₁'), x2 straight up (arrow tip labeled 'x₂'), x3 toward the lower-left front (arrow tip labeled 'x₃')
Panel c) — dashed black axis segments ONLY on the portions of the negative axes that are actually hidden behind a plane (occlusion cue), solid elsewhere
Panel c) — large light-gray plane facing the viewer (hyperplane x₃ = 0, spanned by x1 and x2)
Panel c) — teal vertical plane (hyperplane x₁ = 0, spanned by x2 and x3) crossing the gray plane
Panel c) — terracotta/orange horizontal plane (hyperplane x₂ = 0, spanned by x1 and x3)
Panel c) — black dot at the common origin where all three hyperplanes intersect
Panel letters 'a)', 'b)', 'c)' in black at the tight upper-left corner of each panel
Small draggable input-point marker x = (x₁, x₂, x₃) with a coordinate readout and per-neuron sign readout (added interactive element)
Weight-vector arrow w drawn from the origin perpendicular to the teal hyperplane, showing the normal direction (added interactive element)
Optional faint tint of the positive half-space on one side of the teal hyperplane (added interactive element, off by default)

interactions.teaches: A hyperplane always has one dimension fewer than the input space: a point in 1D, a line in 2D, a plane in 3D — and seeing all three side by side makes the progression explicit.
interactions.label: Input space

interactions.teaches: w₁ is the x₁-component of the weight vector; the boundary is always perpendicular to w, so changing w₁ tips the boundary away from the x₁ axis.
interactions.label: w₁ (teal neuron)

interactions.teaches: w₂ adds an x₂-component to the weight vector, rotating the teal boundary in the x₁–x₂ plane — the boundary direction is fully determined by the ratio of the weight components, not by their magnitude.
interactions.label: w₂ (teal neuron)

interactions.teaches: In 3D the weight vector has three components; tilting w out of the x₁–x₂ plane swings the teal hyperplane into a new orientation while it still passes through the origin.
interactions.label: w₃ (teal neuron, 3D only)

interactions.teaches: The bias shifts the hyperplane along its own normal without rotating it — b = 0 is what makes every boundary in the source figure pass through the origin.
interactions.label: bias b (teal neuron)

interactions.teaches: The hyperplane splits input space into a positive and a negative half-space; revealing the tint shows which side of the boundary makes the pre-activation positive.
interactions.label: Tint positive half-space

interactions.teaches: Where an input lands relative to each boundary fixes the sign of that neuron's pre-activation; the combination of signs is the region the input belongs to.
interactions.label: Drag the input point

interactions.teaches: Orbiting confirms the 3D boundaries are flat 2D sheets slicing space, and that the weight vector stands perpendicular to its own sheet from any viewing angle.

demo_steps.title: a) 1D: the hyperplane is a point
demo_steps.narration: With a single input x₁, the pre-activation w₁x₁ + b changes sign at exactly one location. That point is the hyperplane — a 0-dimensional boundary in a 1-dimensional space.

demo_steps.title: Sign of w₁ flips the half-spaces
demo_steps.narration: Turning on the tint and making w₁ negative swaps which side of the point counts as positive. The boundary itself has not moved — only the direction the weight points.

demo_steps.title: b) 2D: two neurons, two lines
demo_steps.narration: With inputs (x₁, x₂), each neuron's boundary is a line through the origin. Teal is the hyperplane of the first neuron (w = (1,0), so the line is x₁ = 0); orange is a second neuron's.

demo_steps.title: The line is perpendicular to w
demo_steps.narration: Adding an x₂-component to the weight vector rotates the teal line. Watch the weight arrow: the boundary stays exactly perpendicular to it, so the weights choose the boundary's orientation.

demo_steps.title: Bias slides the line off the origin
demo_steps.narration: Changing b translates the boundary along the normal direction without rotating it. Setting b back to zero returns to the figure's origin-crossing arrangement.

demo_steps.title: c) 3D: hyperplanes become planes
demo_steps.narration: In three dimensions each neuron's boundary is a flat plane through the origin. Orbit the view and drag the input point to read the sign of each neuron's pre-activation.

demo_steps.title: Tilt the plane with w₃
demo_steps.narration: Giving the weight vector an x₃-component swings the teal plane out of its original orientation; it remains a flat 2D sheet, one dimension below the 3D input space.

demo_steps.title: All three together
demo_steps.narration: Side by side, the pattern is clear: point in 1D, line in 2D, plane in 3D — the boundary always has one dimension fewer than the input space.

plan.geometry_notes:
World scale: each panel occupies a local frame with axes spanning ±3 world units; the black origin dot is a sphere of radius 0.07. The draggable input-point marker is a small sphere of radius 0.05 (deliberately SMALLER than the origin dot so it never competes with it), colored dark gray #444444 with a thin white outline.

Panel a): single horizontal line along X from (-3,0,0) to (3,0,0), black #000000, stroke ~0.045 thick, cone arrowheads (length 0.28, radius 0.10) at both ends. Italic serif label 'x₁' placed immediately to the RIGHT of and slightly below the +X arrow tip, ~22px on screen. Teal bar centered at the origin: 0.12 wide in X × 0.70 tall in Y, color #86CFC6, drawn behind the black origin dot. Panel letter 'a)' in black at the tight upper-left of the panel bounding box, ~20px, offset only ~0.15 units in from the left edge and ~0.15 below the top.

Panel b): x1 axis horizontal from (-3,0,0) to (3,0,0) with 'x₁' beside the right arrow tip; x2 axis vertical from (0,-3,0) to (0,3,0) with 'x₂' beside the top arrow tip, both black with double cone arrowheads. Teal hyperplane line (neuron 1, default w=(1,0), b=0 → the line x₁=0) lies exactly ON the x2 axis from y=-2.6 to y=+2.6, stroke ~0.10 thick, #86CFC6. Terracotta hyperplane line (neuron 2, x₂=0) lies exactly ON the x1 axis from x=-2.4 to x=+2.4, same thickness, #CE6F4E. Black origin dot drawn on top of both. Panel letter 'b)' at the tight upper-left.

Panel c): three coordinate planes, each 4.5 × 4.5 world units, all through the origin. Light-gray plane #C7CAC9 = x₃ = 0 (spanned by X and Y, facing the viewer, drawn largest and furthest back). Teal plane #86CFC6 = x₁ = 0 (spanned by Y and Z, vertical; its top edge exits upper-right, bottom edge exits lower-left in the source view). Terracotta plane #CE6F4E = x₂ = 0 (spanned by X and Z, horizontal; extends left-front and right-rear). Axis directions exactly as drawn in the source: +x₁ to screen-right, +x₂ straight up, +x₃ toward the lower-left front of the viewer; the arrow going to the upper-right rear is the −x₃ direction. Axis segments are drawn DASHED ONLY on the sub-segments that are genuinely occluded by one of the planes (compute the plane intersections along each axis and split the line there); everywhere else they are solid. Planes semi-transparent (opacity ~0.72) so crossings read. Panel letter 'c)' at the tight upper-left.

'All panels' layout: the three panel frames share one horizontal baseline, centered at X = −8.5, X = 0, X = +8.5 world units respectively, each keeping its own ±3 local span; camera dollies back so the three fit with a small margin, and orbit is limited to a shallow ±15° so the comparison stays legible.

Labels: italic serif math typography (Computer-Modern-like), ~22px for x₁/x₂/x₃, ~20px for the panel letters, pure black #000000, placed adjacent to arrow tips with a gap of ~0.2 world units. Background pure white #FFFFFF.

Math: the teal neuron's pre-activation is z = w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + w₃x₃ + b. Its hyperplane is the set z = 0 (in 1D the point x₁ = −b/w₁; in 2D the line through −b·w/|w|² with direction perpendicular to w; in 3D the plane with unit normal w/|w| at signed distance −b/|w| from the origin). Defaults w = (1, 0, 0), b = 0 reproduce the source exactly. The weight arrow is drawn from the closest point of the hyperplane to the origin, along w/|w|, length fixed at 1.2 world units (magnitude is not encoded, only direction) with a small cone tip, colored #1F7A70. The positive half-space, when enabled, is tinted with the teal color at 12% alpha and clipped to within 2.6 units of the origin so it never dominates the composition; it is OFF by default. The orange neuron in panels b) and c) is fixed at w = (0,1,0), b = 0 and is not driven by the sliders.

authoredPrompt: This figure illustrates how individual neurons in a shallow neural network define hyperplane decision boundaries in input spaces of increasing dimension, across three side-by-side panels labeled a), b), and c). Panel a) shows a one-dimensional input space with a horizontal number line labeled x_1 and a single point (the origin dot) marking where the linear threshold function crosses zero, representing a hyperplane as a point in 1D. Panel b) shows a two-dimensional input space with axes x_1 and x_2 and two colored lines passing through the origin: a vertical teal line and a horizontal orange-terracotta line, each representing a separate hyperplane boundary that divides the 2D plane into two half-spaces. Panel c) shows a three-dimensional input space with axes x_1, x_2, and x_3, rendered as a perspective cube with a light gray front face and teal side face, where the flat face of the cube represents a plane slicing through 3D space — the hyperplane in 3D. The figure demonstrates how the linear pre-activation of a neuron defines a hyperplane that separates input space into two regions, with the dimensionality of the hyperplane being one less than the input dimensionality.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for weight w: tilt the orientation of a selected hyperplane by adjusting one weight component and watch the shaded positive/negative classification regions update in the plot
- Drag an input point (x1, x2, x3): move the point through the 3D feature space and show which side of each neuron's hyperplane it falls on, with the final output class updating to reflect the combined decisions

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: axes span ±3 world units in every panel; the origin dot is a black sphere/disc of radius ~0.07. Panel a) single horizontal line along +/-X from (-3,0,0) to (3,0,0) with cone arrowheads at both ends, 'x_1' label placed just below-right of the +X arrowhead; teal bar centered at origin, ~0.12 wide (X) × 0.7 tall (Y), drawn behind the black dot. Panel b) x1 axis horizontal (-3..3) labeled at right below the arrow, x2 axis vertical (-3..3) labeled at top-right of the arrow; teal hyperplane line lies exactly ON the x2 axis from y=-2.6 to 2.6 with stroke ~0.10 thick; terracotta hyperplane line lies exactly ON the x1 axis from x=-2.4 to 2.4, same thickness; the black origin dot is drawn on top of both. Panel c) three coordinate planes each 4.5 × 4.5 world units, all passing through the origin: light-gray plane = x3 = 0 (spanned by X and Y, faces the viewer, drawn largest and furthest back), teal plane = x1 = 0 (spanned by Y and Z, vertical, its top edge exits above-right and its bottom edge exits below-left in the source view), terracotta plane = x2 = 0 (spanned by X and Z, horizontal, extends to the left-front and right-rear). Axis directions as drawn: +x1 to screen-right, +x2 straight up, +x3 toward the lower-left front of the viewer; the dashed arrow going to the upper-right rear is the -x3 (back) direction, and dashed stubs also mark -x1 at left and -x2 below origin where those axes pass behind the gray plane. Planes are semi-transparent (opacity ~0.75) so crossings are visible. Colors: teal #86CFC6, terracotta/orange #CE6F4E, light gray #C7CAC9, axes and labels pure black #000000, white background #FFFFFF. Math: neuron pre-activation z = w1*x1 + w2*x2 + w3*x3 + b with b = 0 by default so every hyperplane passes through the origin; the hyperplane is the set z = 0, positive half-space tinted with the hyperplane's own color at ~18% alpha, negative half-space left white/untinted. The tiltWeight slider drives the selected neuron's first free weight component (e.g. w1 for the teal plane), so the plane normal rotates from vertical toward the axis as |w| grows.
interactionPlan.notes: Render axes as THREE.Line/CylinderGeometry shafts plus ConeGeometry arrowheads; dashed hidden segments via LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances(). Draw panel b) lines as thin extruded quads or Line2/LineMaterial so their thickness matches the source stroke weight. Planes: PlaneGeometry with DoubleSide, transparent, depthWrite false and renderOrder set so intersections read cleanly; add a thin darker edge outline (EdgesGeometry) to define each plane's silhouette. Labels x_1, x_2, x_3 and a)/b)/c) as CSS2DRenderer/sprite labels with italic serif math styling. Only one panel exists in the scene at a time — swap groups on the dimensionPanel toggle with a short cross-fade, keeping the origin fixed so the progression 1D→2D→3D reads as a growth of the same space. Draggable point: a small sphere constrained to the current panel's space (x1 axis only in a), the XY plane in b), free XYZ in c) via a drag plane facing the camera plus a shift-modifier for depth); on drag, recompute sign(z) for each neuron and update half-space tints, a per-neuron sign readout, and a final output-class chip. Orbit is disabled/locked front-on for panels a) and b) and enabled in panel c). Keep lighting flat (ambient + hemisphere) with MeshBasicMaterial-like flat colors to match the vector-art source.

discrepancies: Panel a) is dominated by a large pale teal 'positive half-space' rectangle and a blue draggable input point that do not exist in the source, which changes the at-a-glance look of the otherwise minimal source panel (a bare axis with a small teal tick at the origin).

The x₁ axis label in the generated panel a) is small and sits well below/right of the arrowhead, whereas the source uses a prominent italic math label sitting right beside the arrow tip; panel letter 'a)' is also far from the axis compared with the source's tight left margin placement.

The source shows all three panels a), b), c) simultaneously side-by-side for direct dimensional comparison; the generated figure only shows one at a time behind the dimension toggle, so the 1D→2D→3D progression is not visible at a glance.

The teal marker in source panel a) is a short bar straddling the axis at the origin; the generated bar is coincident with the tint slab edge so it reads as the left border of a shaded region rather than as an isolated boundary marker.

In the source, panel c)'s negative x₁ branch is drawn dashed only where it is hidden behind the gray plane; the generated figure draws entire negative branches dashed, weakening the occlusion cue that conveys depth.
evaluation.notes: Geometrically faithful reconstruction of the three hyperplane panels (correct plane orientations, cone-tipped axes, dashed hidden branches) with a rich, well-wired interaction set (dimension toggle, neuron selection, weight slider, draggable input point, guided demo), but the default 1D view is visually cluttered by an added half-space tint slab and input point not in the source, and the axis labels are undersized/offset relative to the source's prominent italic math labels.
action_items: Increase axis-label font size (≈22px) and move x₁/x₂/x₃ labels adjacent to the arrow tips to match the source's prominent italic math typography; tighten the 'a)/b)/c)' panel letters to the upper-left of each panel.

Default the 'Tint positive half-space' checkbox to off (or reduce its extent/opacity) so the initial view matches the source's clean axis-plus-teal-bar composition, and shrink the input-point sphere so it does not compete with the origin dot.
In panel c), clip or mask the dashed negative axis segments so they are dashed only where actually occluded by a plane, reproducing the source's occlusion cue.
Consider a 'show all panels' option that lays a), b), c) side-by-side so the 1D→2D→3D progression matches the source's comparative layout.
plan_action_items: Reconsider mapping a single scalar 'Weight w' slider to a 25°-per-unit rotation of the 2D/3D boundary — expose the actual weight components (w₁, w₂, w₃) or label the control 'rotate boundary' so the weight-vector/normal relationship is not misrepresented.

demo_steps.title: a) 1D: the hyperplane is a point
demo_steps.narration: With a single input x₁, the pre-activation w₁x₁ + b changes sign at exactly one location. That point is the hyperplane — a 0-dimensional boundary in a 1-dimensional space.

demo_steps.title: Sign of w₁ flips the half-spaces
demo_steps.narration: Turning on the tint and making w₁ negative swaps which side of the point counts as positive. The boundary itself has not moved — only the direction the weight points.

demo_steps.title: b) 2D: two neurons, two lines
demo_steps.narration: With inputs (x₁, x₂), each neuron's boundary is a line through the origin. Teal is the hyperplane of the first neuron (w = (1,0), so the line is x₁ = 0); orange is a second neuron's.

demo_steps.title: The line is perpendicular to w
demo_steps.narration: Adding an x₂-component to the weight vector rotates the teal line. Watch the weight arrow: the boundary stays exactly perpendicular to it, so the weights choose the boundary's orientation.

demo_steps.title: Bias slides the line off the origin
demo_steps.narration: Changing b translates the boundary along the normal direction without rotating it. Setting b back to zero returns to the figure's origin-crossing arrangement.

demo_steps.title: c) 3D: hyperplanes become planes
demo_steps.narration: In three dimensions each neuron's boundary is a flat plane through the origin. Orbit the view and drag the input point to read the sign of each neuron's pre-activation.

demo_steps.title: Tilt the plane with w₃
demo_steps.narration: Giving the weight vector an x₃-component swings the teal plane out of its original orientation; it remains a flat 2D sheet, one dimension below the 3D input space.

demo_steps.title: All three together
demo_steps.narration: Side by side, the pattern is clear: point in 1D, line in 2D, plane in 3D — the boundary always has one dimension fewer than the input space.

plan.geometry_notes:
World scale: each panel occupies a local frame with axes spanning ±3 world units; the black origin dot is a sphere of radius 0.07. The draggable input-point marker is a small sphere of radius 0.05 (deliberately SMALLER than the origin dot so it never competes with it), colored dark gray #444444 with a thin white outline.

Panel a): single horizontal line along X from (-3,0,0) to (3,0,0), black #000000, stroke ~0.045 thick, cone arrowheads (length 0.28, radius 0.10) at both ends. Italic serif label 'x₁' placed immediately to the RIGHT of and slightly below the +X arrow tip, ~22px on screen. Teal bar centered at the origin: 0.12 wide in X × 0.70 tall in Y, color #86CFC6, drawn behind the black origin dot. Panel letter 'a)' in black at the tight upper-left of the panel bounding box, ~20px, offset only ~0.15 units in from the left edge and ~0.15 below the top.

Panel b): x1 axis horizontal from (-3,0,0) to (3,0,0) with 'x₁' beside the right arrow tip; x2 axis vertical from (0,-3,0) to (0,3,0) with 'x₂' beside the top arrow tip, both black with double cone arrowheads. Teal hyperplane line (neuron 1, default w=(1,0), b=0 → the line x₁=0) lies exactly ON the x2 axis from y=-2.6 to y=+2.6, stroke ~0.10 thick, #86CFC6. Terracotta hyperplane line (neuron 2, x₂=0) lies exactly ON the x1 axis from x=-2.4 to x=+2.4, same thickness, #CE6F4E. Black origin dot drawn on top of both. Panel letter 'b)' at the tight upper-left.

Panel c): three coordinate planes, each 4.5 × 4.5 world units, all through the origin. Light-gray plane #C7CAC9 = x₃ = 0 (spanned by X and Y, facing the viewer, drawn largest and furthest back). Teal plane #86CFC6 = x₁ = 0 (spanned by Y and Z, vertical; its top edge exits upper-right, bottom edge exits lower-left in the source view). Terracotta plane #CE6F4E = x₂ = 0 (spanned by X and Z, horizontal; extends left-front and right-rear). Axis directions exactly as drawn in the source: +x₁ to screen-right, +x₂ straight up, +x₃ toward the lower-left front of the viewer; the arrow going to the upper-right rear is the −x₃ direction. Axis segments are drawn DASHED ONLY on the sub-segments that are genuinely occluded by one of the planes (compute the plane intersections along each axis and split the line there); everywhere else they are solid. Planes semi-transparent (opacity ~0.72) so crossings read. Panel letter 'c)' at the tight upper-left.

'All panels' layout: the three panel frames share one horizontal baseline, centered at X = −8.5, X = 0, X = +8.5 world units respectively, each keeping its own ±3 local span; camera dollies back so the three fit with a small margin, and orbit is limited to a shallow ±15° so the comparison stays legible.

Labels: italic serif math typography (Computer-Modern-like), ~22px for x₁/x₂/x₃, ~20px for the panel letters, pure black #000000, placed adjacent to arrow tips with a gap of ~0.2 world units. Background pure white #FFFFFF.

Math: the teal neuron's pre-activation is z = w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + w₃x₃ + b. Its hyperplane is the set z = 0 (in 1D the point x₁ = −b/w₁; in 2D the line through −b·w/|w|² with direction perpendicular to w; in 3D the plane with unit normal w/|w| at signed distance −b/|w| from the origin). Defaults w = (1, 0, 0), b = 0 reproduce the source exactly. The weight arrow is drawn from the closest point of the hyperplane to the origin, along w/|w|, length fixed at 1.2 world units (magnitude is not encoded, only direction) with a small cone tip, colored #1F7A70. The positive half-space, when enabled, is tinted with the teal color at 12% alpha and clipped to within 2.6 units of the origin so it never dominates the composition; it is OFF by default. The orange neuron in panels b) and c) is fixed at w = (0,1,0), b = 0 and is not driven by the sliders.
